- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–7 days.
- Model underestimates true price volatility when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast for next 5–10 days.
- If model forecast is below 60% of recent 18-day high, and sentiment is positive, increase forecast by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rally.
- When sentiment is positive but recent price is flat, model tends to lag; forecast should be 0.5–1.0% above recent 5-day average.
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of 30-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly negative; use sentiment as trigger for floor correction.
